page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It allocates 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. Hardware acceleration features include Intel AMX (amx_tile, amx_int8), AVX-512 vector extensions (f, vnni, bf16), and cryptographic acceleration through AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instructions.

The instance delivers 768.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high density of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include discrete GPUs or integrated local disk storage, relying on network-attached Premium Storage for persistent file systems. In synthetic memory testing, the instance demonstrates strong performance, delivering 187.67 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 116.85 GB/sec for large-block writes, positioning memory transfer rates in the upper quartile of benchmarked machines.

Processing evaluations show top-tier single-core execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 2142.0 and strong throughput in text and image processing tasks. Multi-core operations perform in the median tier, returning a Geekbench multi-core score of 15298.0 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 23968.2. Redis in-memory key-value processing reaches 35.07 million SET operations per second, while small-model LLM inference achieves 294.92 tokens per second for text generation using 135M parameter models.

By constraining vCPU count while retaining full physical host memory scale, the E96-24s_v6 improves qualitative cost efficiency for workloads governed by per-core software licensing. The absence of local disk requires planning for remote I/O latency. This hardware profile is appropriate for large-footprint in-memory databases, Redis caches, enterprise SAP or ERP engines, and intensive memory-bound data analytics pipelines.
